doc: match_to_earth(cov, earth, hadley_deg, levels, strength): sigmas 2^k (k < levels) in Earth texels, scaled by the width ratio for the generated map; band_layers of both (float32), each generated layer quantile-matched per latitude zone to the same Earth layer (_match_by_zone, Earth zones from lat at hadley 30 with rows past 67.5 degrees excluded), summed with strength * matched + (1 - strength) * original, plus the matched residual, clipped to [0, 1], then matched once more as a whole to Earth's own map, and blended again by strength; the result is float32. Extra output block_mean8 = float64 means of the 8x8 blocks of `out`, computed by the case: a robust summary that bounds the texels `out` lets differ. Tolerance: no blurred layer feeds the quantile tables here, so the f32 pipeline and a float64 one agree to 6e-8: the golden float32 tolerance, no outliers. The stored map reaches the tables as it is, and its tied texels sit on plateaus: a one-ulp change of the INPUT moves the output by up to 8e-2 through the 1e-9 ladder, so hand the function exactly the stored values. A cloudless 64x32 map (all 0): every layer is 0, every quantile table is a flat run of 0 (the + 1e-9 k ladder), so each interp lands on dst[0] of the zone and the result is a mix of Earth's lowest quantiles. A flat input is where the tables are most fragile (do not nudge it: a texel off the plateau climbs the ladder). Input convention: the u8 input(s) cov, earth are maps stored as bytes, and the function receives them as float32(u8) / float32(255) (`u8.astype(np.float32) / 255.0`: the division is done, and correctly rounded, in float32, as measure.load reads an 8-bit map), NOT as the raw bytes and NOT as a float64 quotient (a texel on a histogram edge or a threshold would move). params.u8_inputs lists them.

u8_inputs.cov: float32(u8) / float32(255), the division in float32
u8_inputs.earth: float32(u8) / float32(255), the division in float32
